title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake pornographic videos were created and hosted on a platform that received millions of monthly visitors. The videos used the faces of named Dutch public figures without their consent, placing them in explicit sexual content. This is a failure of platform moderation, where illegal material remained accessible to the public and generated revenue through view counts.

The deployment failure was the absence of any effective system to prevent upload or detect and remove non-consensual intimate imagery. Whether the platform had detection tools, human review processes, or other safeguards is not established from the reporting. It would have required either automated detection of deepfake pornography before publication, human review of uploads, or rapid removal upon report and complaint.

The material violated Dutch law as revenge porn and caused harm documented enough that victims filed police reports and considered legal action. What remains unknown is whether the platform operator knowingly permitted the content, whether adequate technical or procedural safeguards existed, or what enforcement actions resulted from the reports filed.

summary:
Several female Dutch celebrities are considering legal action after discovering themselves in fake pornographic videos posted on an online platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The platform contains manipulated videos featuring Dutch artists, television presenters, Olympic athletes, current and former government ministers, mayors, and members of the royal family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and urged victims to file reports with authorities.

Deepfake pornography, which digitally places a person's head onto explicit content, constitutes revenge porn and is illegal under Dutch law. Managers and representatives of various victims have confirmed they have filed reports or are considering legal action. Users who upload the material are advised to remain anonymous, likely to avoid prosecution, and are paid more when videos receive higher view counts. Legal experts recommend victims file reports, potentially allowing prosecutors to shut down the website, or pursue other options including class action lawsuits or complaints to data protection authorities.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
